title: What Did I Just See? Paranormal Activity on Broadway! Hold on to your glass!
transcript: Paranormal Activity is a damn good hybrid of theater and haunted house thrills. It's not great theater by any stretch, but it is a well-acted, impressively executed ghost story that will likely scare the bejesus out of you. We're not safe. You believe me now? It's an offshoot of Oren Peli's supernatural horror franchise that started in 2007, spawning seven films in total with an eighth on the way. The stage incarnation, written by Levi Holloway, is a tightly structured four-character yarn, centering on a young American couple freshly arrived in London after experiencing a number of unexplained episodes in Chicago. James and his wife Lou, played by Travis A. Knight and Shar Alvarez, soon discover that the disturbances haven't gone away. In fact, they've gotten worse. Lou, who's been plagued by the strange happenings, gets little support from her atheist husband who dismisses the supernatural, leaving her to secretly live through antidepressants. And we're left to wonder if this is a match made in heaven or hell. Knight and Alvarez, both making their Broadway debuts, are fine actors turning in excellent performances as the beleaguered couple. We're also introduced to James cloyingly intrusive mother from Florida and a popular psychic, both providing key pieces of the puzzle. But the play's not really the thing here. It's the technical sleight of hand designed by Chris Fisher to induce all manner of frights. Right from the start, there's a shock to the system with a blast of chords that gets the blood pumping, and we're off. With no spoilers, there's a steady stream of chilling scenes and sounds courtesy of a first-rate special effects team led by director Felix Barrett. He's best known for his marvelously immersive Sleep No More. To their collective credit, the technical crew achieved the maximum impact as the decibel level of audience screams never flagged. I hope I am a little crazy. As ghost stories go, it's not perfect. The twist ending is too abrupt and the dimly lit set prevented some in the audience from catching the climactic finale. But small qualms for a show that mostly gets the job done. At the outset, I said I'm not a screamer and I can honestly say I didn't scream once, but I did jump quite a few times. And that prompts a warning. Drinks are served in glassware. Sudden jerking bodies next to fragile glass can lead to unintended consequences, so beware in more ways than one. I'm Roma Torre for 5th Row Center
